added_test_titles: test "transport-sanitizes non-json-safe tool payloads" do
test "sanitize_telemetry_metadata redacts, bounds, and summarizes payload fields" do
test "sanitize_telemetry_metadata does not inspect unexpected payload terms" do
test "sanitize_transport_payload produces bounded JSON-safe data" do

v3_tests: examples/v3/test/examples/02_requests/02_06_output_contract_test.exs::output telemetry is correlated and has no model payload
examples/v3/test/examples/02_requests/02_06_output_contract_test.exs::DSL, data, Builder and JSON keep output telemetry while disabling delta capture
examples/v3/test/examples/02_requests/02_06_output_contract_test.exs::disabled telemetry keeps request events and invalid flags fail before admission
examples/v3/test/examples/02_requests/02_06_output_contract_test.exs::validated event previews redact map keys and bound Unicode values
examples/v3/test/examples/02_requests/02_08_error_contract_test.exs::output error summaries terminate for null fields and redact bounded payloads
examples/v3/test/examples/02_requests/02_08_error_contract_test.exs::arbitrary repair error details produce a committed failure with portable metadata
examples/v3/test/examples/02_requests/02_09_tool_results_test.exs::nonportable tool values have bounded model and stored inspection forms
examples/v3/test/examples/14_resume/14_06_trace_and_cycles_test.exs::tool start redaction true leaves the real tool input intact

examples/v3/test/examples/14_resume/14_06_trace_and_cycles_test.exs::native Agent DSL applies the same tool event setting
commits.decision: Retain one explicit sanitizer with telemetry and transport profiles, key redaction, bounded metadata and JSON-safe tool content. Prove boundary behavior for unusual keys, tuples, error summaries and mandatory correlation.

source_review_details.notes: Read complete source/docs/tests/mix diff, PR 300 and issue 265. Observe emit/span start apply telemetry profile; tool JSON applies transport. Redaction-only API remains distinct. Final source leaves binary keys unchanged, processes all tuple elements and full list lengths, can revisit nil type/message error maps, and inserts mandatory metadata before truncation without reserving it. These source-level gaps require bounded acceptance tests; no runtime reproduction or fix claimed. Tool_result later switches value mode with telemetry limits, not full transport defaults.
source_review_details.discussion_scope: Complete selected diffs and all associated PR discussion; issues 265, 294, 307 and 326; relevant final source. Reported consumer bridge unavailable through GitHub contents API. No production edits or runtime tests.

v3_evidence.result: 196 acceptance tests pass. Tool results with process IDs, references and sensitive nested keys use one bounded transport projection for model JSON and portable request inspection.

commits.decision: Preserve explicit runtime Agent Skills integration, one scoped catalog, stable session activation and genuine instruction retention through compaction. Use final lazy loading, define trusted request bindings and session cleanup, and prove actual transcript provenance, call/result pairing and repeated instruction handling.

source_review_details.notes: Read the complete 2918-line merged diff, all PR 325 feedback and issue 323. Retain the scoped-miss fallback and bare-relative-path fixes. The initial eager runtime body reads are superseded by metadata-only catalog work. Final per-request tool context and dynamic tool maps can change reserved bindings; migration must define trusted host scope. Session bookkeeping alone neither deduplicates instruction text nor ensures automatic owner cleanup. Runner provenance, projected refs and compaction are separately tested in v2; v3 must connect them through real transport. Source checks identify conflicting assistant-copy, mutable Action-map, imported-ref and transcript-order cases; no runtime reproduction is claimed.
source_review_details.discussion_scope: Complete merged diff, complete associated PR discussion and linked local user reports; relevant final source and test context checked. Later catalog/resource commits retain separate pending full reviews. No production edits or runtime tests.

v3_evidence.result: All 28 context-operation integration cases pass. The linked cases retain request refs in core Thread messages, apply a portable pending operation once on recovery, commit replacement/prompt/applied-ID together despite a lost durable completion reply, and preserve accepted skill call/result pairs through the next real HTTP request. Conflicting assistant copies cannot change retained names or arguments.
v3_evidence.limits: Compaction trusts host-imported accepted current history. Actual LoadSkill identity/callback provenance, tenant/catalog isolation, skill resources and binary providers remain required. Thread history is subject to Agent state-size limits; deduplication keeps only the last128 IDs. Old Agent conversion, complete storage/failure cases, CLI and package/consumer/runtime-floor/migration/rollback gates remain open. All history statuses remain pending.

v3_evidence.result: All 27 new integration cases pass. Real Actions, approved tool results, committed history, compaction and later provider requests are connected. Cases prove scoped catalogues, owned activation, fresh bounded resources, image/PDF transport and cleanup/restore. A separate v3 command passes 293 retained skill/resource checks.
v3_evidence.limits: Explicit host context supplies the prepared catalogue. Legacy agent_skills authoring, automatic index/tools, all source forms, standalone skill continuation, installed application and CLI tests, complete conversion/recovery, root package/consumer/runtime-floor/migration/rollback remain required. Concurrent provider callbacks are not exactly once. Imported accepted history remains host-trusted. All history statuses remain pending.

v3_evidence.result: All 21 integration cases pass. Public agent_skills, native skills DSL, source data, Builder and JSON share runtime catalogue preparation. Real HTTP traces prove lazy activation, selected module Actions, per-profile scope, runtime directory resolution, strict current-file validation, restore and live tool/prompt changes. Public automatic tools retain configured timeout/retry defaults. A separate v3 command passes 293 retained skill/resource tests.
v3_evidence.limits: Automatic skills require a live ReAct Session. Static sources use MFA callbacks; manual preparation retains runtime callback forms. Module Plugins remain explicit Agent declarations. Pure configuration views exclude transient index/catalogue preparation. Standalone continuation, installed resources/CLI, complete Agent conversion/recovery and root package/consumer/minimum-runtime/migration/rollback gates remain open. All history statuses remain pending.

v3_evidence.result: All 11 integration cases pass. Public defaults, raw Signals, live/direct replacement, request precedence, admitted context snapshots, callbacks, tool projection, native/data/Builder/JSON forms, profile scope and restore use one Configuration Plugin. Captured HTTP requests contain the expected real tool results. Invalid base maps do not change committed state.
v3_evidence.limits: Base values must be portable and cannot replace reserved runtime or skill bindings. Request values remain transient. This does not close standalone skill continuation, parent Strategy retirement, complete Agent state conversion/recovery, or root package/consumer/minimum-runtime/migration/rollback acceptance. All history statuses remain pending.

commits.decision: Preserve Agent-only tool transforms, immutable identity, callback order and canonical result/effect handling; prove ReAct and ToT boundaries with the reported alias workflow and ordinary direct Action calls.

source_review_details.notes: Full production/test/guide diff and PR 347 complete discussion. Final maintainer note supersedes proposed ToolRuntime/inbound-signal claims: ToT transforms after raw executor delivery. Shared ToolInterceptor validates identity and canonical triples, catches exceptions/throws/exits and filters effects. ReAct applies after hooks after parallel results collection; failure cannot undo tools. Pending work re-enters preparation, so retry counts do not prove once-only restore semantics. Later target changes leave these runner/interceptor/ToT boundaries intact.
source_review_details.discussion_scope: Complete associated PR descriptions, issue comments, reviews and inline comments. Linked local and MCP reports and final source behavior are recorded in review 05. No production implementation or dynamic baseline tests ran.

v3_evidence.result: 263 acceptance tests pass, including 32 callback examples. The PR 347 alias workflow uses real Actions and explicit candidate state. Native/public Agent callbacks retain identity, before-validation order, retry counts, ordered collection, final errors, policy, trusted runtime context, cancellation and deadlines. Data/Builder/source-JSON and literal Flow tools execute the same path. Eleven retained ToolInterceptor tests also pass.
v3_evidence.limits: ToT raw inbound tool-result semantics and its alias path, standalone AI tool facades, pending-work validation and callback replay, durable pause/resume, sink recovery and package checks remain pending.

v3_evidence.result: Both native ToT phases use shared tool execution. Before callbacks rewrite arguments before validation; after callbacks transform canonical results. The example waits for reverse tool completion and proves provider result order. Round and parser-repair limits prevent further tool execution. The common policy also removes repair tools after a request transform.
v3_evidence.limits: This evidence covers the native ToT profile and shared Machine/Result data APIs. Public ToTAgent, namespace helpers, old Strategy callbacks, CLI/capability entry points, the exact PR 347 alias/state workflow and full failure/recovery variants remain pending. Typed ToT output and rich input remain explicit gaps. Root dependency, consumer, runtime-floor, migration and rollback checks are not complete. All historical rows remain pending.

v3_evidence.result: The PR 347 alias workflow now runs through ToT session and ordinary Agent paths with actual list/consume Actions. Before callbacks restore original keys before validation; after callbacks receive raw final retry results and transform model/canonical outputs. Permitted aliases stage until completion. Denied effects, all explicit callback failure modes, and a later callback failure retain real tool evidence without committing earlier staged state. Direct Exec preserves original-key behavior without AI interception.
v3_evidence.limits: Partial public ToT and callback evidence only. Live tree inspection, rich input, typed ToT output, runtime model/state overrides, standalone helpers, capability/CLI paths, complete provider failure variants, pending-work replay and durable recovery remain required. Root dependency, consumer, runtime-floor, migration and rollback gates are open. All historical statuses remain pending.

v3_evidence.result: All 11 integration cases pass. Public defaults, raw Signals, live/direct replacement, request precedence, admitted context snapshots, callbacks, tool projection, native/data/Builder/JSON forms, profile scope and restore use one Configuration Plugin. Captured HTTP requests contain the expected real tool results. Invalid base maps do not change committed state.
v3_evidence.limits: Base values must be portable and cannot replace reserved runtime or skill bindings. Request values remain transient. This does not close standalone skill continuation, parent Strategy retirement, complete Agent state conversion/recovery, or root package/consumer/minimum-runtime/migration/rollback acceptance. All history statuses remain pending.
